mainTopic: The end of the מוציא שם רע discussion, then a new משנה on a father's rights over his daughter compared with a husband's, and the גמרא's sources for the father's right to her קידושין.
overview: First the גמרא challenges an earlier version of רב כהנא's report from רבי יוחנן and gives a corrected version: the husband who defames his bride is liable only if both his relations and his claim are about relations in the normal way. Then a new משנה lists a father's rights over his young daughter: her קידושין, what she finds, her earnings, cancelling her vows and receiving her גט. He does not, however, eat the produce of her property. When she marries, the husband gains more: he eats her produce, and he must feed her, ransom her and bury her. רבי יהודה adds that even the poorest husband must provide two flutes and a mourning woman at her funeral. The גמרא asks how we know the קידושין money goes to the father, and רב יהודה learns it from the פסוק about the freed אמה העבריה. Asked why the money should not go to the girl herself, the גמרא first tries 'בנעוריה בית אביה', but then limits that פסוק to vows and rejects other possible sources. In the end it explains that the אמה פסוק is about a comparable leaving, and that קידושין really is a leaving from the father's authority, at least for vows. Finally, the גמרא learns from 'והיתה לאיש אחר' that קידושין by שטר and ביאה are also in the father's hands, and it begins the clause about what she finds.

steps.title: Both acts must be in the normal way
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects to the earlier version of רב כהנא's report. According to רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, both the husband's relations and the claimed act must be in the normal way.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we need both this one and that one to be in the normal way!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the earlier version of רב כהנא's report. That version doesn't fit רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, who requires both acts to be in the normal way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב reads the פסוקים of מוציא שם רע literally: the husband was with her and found she was not a בתולה. That means two things must both be כדרכה: the husband's own relations with her, and the act he accuses her of. Any version of רבי יוחנן's teaching that allows one of them to be שלא כדרכה cannot match this view.

keyTerms.meaning: This one and that one, meaning both of them
In the normal way of relations

phrases.english: We require both this one and that one to be in the normal way!
phrases.notes: "This one and that one" means the husband's own relations with her, and the act he accuses her of doing with another man.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues from the previous daf. It challenges the earlier version of רב כהנא's report in the name of רבי יוחנן.
steps.kashyaTarget: The earlier version of רב כהנא's report from רבי יוחנן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב needs both acts to be כדרכה. A version that relaxes either one cannot be following him.

steps.title: The corrected version of רבי יוחנן's teaching
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives the correct version of what רב כהנא sent in the name of רבי יוחנן. The husband is liable only if he had relations with her in the normal way and accused her about relations in the normal way.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב כהנא sent this in the name of רבי יוחנן: He is not liable unless he had relations with her in the normal way, and he defamed her about relations in the normal way.
steps.whatsHappening: Because of the question, the גמרא throws out the old version and gives a corrected one. In this version, both acts are in the normal way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אלא tells us the earlier version is dropped. The new version requires both acts to be כדרכה, so it now fits רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. This closes the discussion of מוציא שם רע before the new משנה starts.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; it signals that the earlier version is being replaced
He sent word, as in a message
A husband who falsely accuses his bride of not being a בתולה

steps.whatToRemember: The final version of רבי יוחנן's rule: the husband pays the fine for מוציא שם רע only if both his own relations and the act he accuses her of were כדרכה.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Kahana sent word
in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
He is not liable unless he had relations with her in the normal way,
and he defames her about relations in the normal way.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא שְׁלַח רַב כָּהֲנָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 1 by replacing the report with a corrected version.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Corrects the wording of the report (the teaching is restated in a different form).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The earlier version, which did not require both acts to be כדרכה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both the husband's relations and the act he accuses her of must be כדרכה, which fits רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.

steps.title: A father's rights over his daughter
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists what a father controls or receives from his young daughter. It also notes that he does not eat the produce of her property while she is alive.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A father has rights over his daughter in her קידושין, whether it is done with money, a document or relations. He is entitled to what she finds and to her earnings. He can cancel her vows, and he receives her גט for her. But he does not eat the produce of her property while she is alive.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists the rights a father has over his daughter while she is young.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The father controls her קידושין (and the money of her קידושין goes to him). He also gets her מציאה and her מעשה ידיה, can do הפרת נדרים, and accepts her גט. The last line is a limit: unlike a husband, he does not get פירות from her property during her life.

keyTerms.meaning: Entitled to; has the rights to
Betrothal, the first stage of marriage

steps.whyThisMatters: This list sets up the whole סוגיא that follows. The גמרא will look for a source for each of the father's rights, starting with קידושין money.

phrases.english: MISHNA: A father has rights over his daughter
in her betrothal, whether through money, through a document, or through relations.
He is entitled to what she finds, and to her earnings,
and to cancel her vows, and he receives her bill of divorce.
But he does not eat the produce of her property during her lifetime.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה with a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A father controls his daughter's קידושין, מציאה, מעשה ידיה, vows and גט. He does not get the פירות of her property during her life.

steps.title: A husband gets more than the father had
steps.stepSummary: Once she marries, the husband has more rights than the father. He eats the produce of her property, and he must feed her, ransom her and bury her.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once she is married, the husband has more than the father: he eats the produce of her property while she is alive, and he must provide her food, ransom her if she is captured, and bury her.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה compares the husband to the father. The husband gains a right the father did not have, and he also takes on duties.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line answers the last line of the father's list. The father does not eat פירות during her life, but the husband does. In exchange, the husband must give her מזונות, pay for her פדיון if she is captured, and pay for her קבורה.

keyTerms.meaning: She has married, meaning the full marriage after קידושין
Produce or income from her property

phrases.english: Once she is married, the husband has more than him,
phrases.notes: "Him" is the father from the earlier list.

phrases.english: in that he eats the produce of her property during her lifetime,
and he is obligated to provide her food,
and her ransom, and her burial.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה by comparing the husband to the father.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A husband eats his wife's פירות during her life and is obligated in her מזונות, פדיון and קבורה.

steps.title: The minimum for a wife's funeral
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says that even the poorest Jew must provide at least two flutes and a mourning woman for his wife's funeral.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: Even the poorest man in ישראל should not provide less than two flutes and a woman who sings sad songs.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה adds a detail to the husband's duty of burial. He sets the smallest acceptable funeral.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said the husband must bury his wife. רבי יהודה teaches that burial includes the usual mourning customs, namely flute players and a woman who chants a lament. These are a basic part of the duty, not an extra for the rich.

keyTerms.meaning: The poorest person among the Jewish people
Flutes, which were played at funerals
A woman who chants mourning songs

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
Even the poorest man of the Jewish people
should not provide fewer than two flutes and a woman who laments.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר אֲפִילּוּ עָנִי שֶׁבְּיִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands on the husband's duty of קבורה from step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Burial includes at least two flutes and a מקוננת, even for the poorest husband.

steps.title: Source for the father getting קידושין money
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that the money of a daughter's קידושין belongs to her father.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Money: from where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins on the משנה's first right. It asks for the source that the father receives his daughter's קידושין money. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said the father has rights in her קידושין through money. The גמרא wants a פסוק showing that the money itself goes to him.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know this?

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not how we know קידושין can be done with money. It is how we know the money goes to the father and not to the daughter.

phrases.english: GEMARA: That he is entitled to the money, from where do we derive this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא's analysis of the first clause of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that a daughter's קידושין money belongs to her father.

steps.title: Learned from the freed maidservant
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה learns from the פסוק about a freed עבריה. Her master gets no money when she leaves him, which implies that another "master", her father, does get money when she leaves him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: The פסוק says, "She shall go out for free, without money." There is no money for this master, but there is money for a different master. And who is that? Her father.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers the question with a דיוק from a פסוק about a Hebrew maidservant who goes free.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק stresses that when the עבריה leaves her master, he gets no money. רב יהודה reads this as limited to "this master": there is another master over a girl who does get money when she leaves him. That is her father, who receives money when she leaves his authority through קידושין.
steps.confusionAlert: רב יהודה in the גמרא is an אמורא. He is not the same person as רבי יהודה, the תנא quoted in the משנה.
steps.whatToRemember: The father gets his daughter's קידושין money. This is learned from "וְיָצְאָה חִנָּם אֵין כָּסֶף": no money for this master, but there is money for another master, her father.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said: The verse states:
"Then she shall go out for nothing, without money,"
there is no money for this master,
but there is money for a different master,
and who is that? Her father.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: From "וְיָצְאָה חִנָּם אֵין כָּסֶף": no money goes to the maidservant's master, which implies money does go to another master, her father, when she leaves his authority through קידושין.

steps.title: Maybe the money goes to the girl herself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the עבריה פסוק could mean the קידושין money belongs to the girl, not her father.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say the money belongs to her!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב יהודה's reading from Step 7. It sets up the challenge that the money might go to the girl herself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 said: no money for this master implies money for another 'master', the father. But the implied 'someone who gets money' could just as easily be the girl herself.

phrases.english: But say it goes to her!
phrases.notes: He means the קידושין money: maybe the girl keeps it, not her father.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the inference drawn in Step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's inference that the money goes to the father
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The inference only shows that someone other than the master gets money. That someone could be the girl.

steps.title: The father accepts her קידושין, so he takes the money
steps.stepSummary: Since the Torah shows the father gives his daughter in marriage, it makes no sense that she takes the money.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now, her father accepts her קידושין, as it says 'I gave my daughter to this man.' Would she then take the money?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers Step 8. The father is the one who marries her off, so the money naturally goes to him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק 'את בתי נתתי לאיש הזה' shows that the father is the one who gives his daughter in קידושין. It would be strange for him to carry out the קידושין while she collects the money.

keyTerms.meaning: Now, consider (opens a 'how could it be' argument)

phrases.english: Now, her father accepts her betrothal,
as it is written: 'I gave my daughter to this man,'
and she takes the money?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Logical argument based on a פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The money might belong to the girl.
steps.terutzMaskana: The father, who accepts the קידושין, receives the money.

steps.title: Maybe this only applies to a young girl
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the father's control applies only to a קטנה. A נערה, who can act legally, should marry herself off and keep the money.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say this applies only to a קטנה, who has no legal 'hand.' A נערה, who does have a 'hand,' should betroth herself and take the money!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer in Step 9. It suggests the rule might apply only to a very young girl.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קטנה cannot do legal acts, so of course her father accepts for her. A נערה can do legal acts herself, so perhaps she accepts her own קידושין and keeps the money.

keyTerms.meaning: A girl in the six months after age 12
'Hand': the legal ability to act for oneself

steps.confusionAlert: Even a נערה is still under her father's authority. Being able to act legally does not by itself free her from him.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵימָא הָנֵי מִילֵּי קְטַנָּה, דְּלֵית לַהּ יָד.
phrases.english: But say this applies only to a minor, who has no 'hand.'
phrases.notes: 'Hand' here means the legal power to make deals and acts for herself.

phrases.english: But a young woman, who does have a 'hand'
should betroth herself
and should take the money herself!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the answer of Step 9 to a קטנה only.
steps.kashyaTarget: The father's right to the money in every case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The argument from 'the father accepts' fits only a girl who cannot act herself. A נערה can act herself.

steps.title: All gains of youth belong to the father
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'בנעוריה בית אביה' teaches that everything a girl gains as a נערה goes to her father.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'in her youth, in her father's house.' All gains of youth go to her father.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers Step 10 with a פסוק. It shows that even a נערה's gains belong to her father.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'נעוריה' points to the stage of נערות. So even though a נערה can act for herself, what she gains in that stage, including קידושין money, belongs to her father.

keyTerms.meaning: In her youth, in her father's house

phrases.english: The verse states: 'In her youth, in her father's house'
all the gains of youth belong to her father.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 10 with a פסוק.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A נערה keeps her own קידושין money.
steps.terutzMaskana: All gains of נערות belong to the father.

steps.title: Then why does רב need a separate source for her earnings?
steps.stepSummary: רב learns that a daughter's earnings go to her father from the אמה פסוק. If 'בנעוריה בית אביה' covers all gains, that source would be unnecessary.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about רב הונא quoting רב: From where do we know a daughter's earnings belong to her father? From 'If a man sells his daughter as a maidservant.' Just as a maidservant's earnings go to her master, so a daughter's earnings go to her father. Why is this needed? Learn it from 'in her youth, in her father's house'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer of Step 11. It brings רב's teaching, which would be pointless if Step 11 were right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'בנעוריה בית אביה' gives the father all gains of youth, it already covers her earnings. So רב's separate derivation from the אמה פסוק shows he did not read that פסוק as being about money.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֶלָּא הָא דְּאָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: But what about that which Rav Huna said Rav said:
From where do we know that a daughter's earnings go to her father?

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְכִי יִמְכּוֹר אִישׁ אֶת בִּתּוֹ לְאָמָה״,
phrases.english: As it says: 'And if a man sells his daughter as a maidservant,'
just as a maidservant's earnings go to her master,
so too a daughter's earnings go to her father.
Why do I need this?
Let him derive it from 'in her youth, in her father's house'!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶלָּא הָא דְּאָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the broad reading given in Step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading 'בנעוריה בית אביה' as covering all money matters
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If that reading were right, רב's separate derivation for earnings would be unnecessary.

steps.title: That פסוק is about cancelling vows
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא retracts. 'בנעוריה בית אביה' is written about הפרת נדרים, not about money.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, that פסוק is written about cancelling vows.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives up the broad reading from Step 11. It explains that the פסוק appears in the section about a father cancelling his daughter's vows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This explains why רב needed the אמה פסוק: 'בנעוריה בית אביה' only shows the father's power over her vows. It does not by itself give him money rights.
steps.whyThisMatters: The answer of Step 11 is now limited. This sets up the next question: why not extend the vow rule to money?

phrases.english: Rather, that phrase
is written about the cancelling of vows.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: הָהוּא בַּהֲפָרַת נְדָרִים הוּא דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves Step 12 by narrowing the פסוק of Step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of a פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'בנעוריה בית אביה' covers all gains of youth.
steps.terutzMaskana: It covers only the father's power over her vows.

steps.title: Money laws are not learned from איסור laws
steps.stepSummary: One might extend the father's power over vows to money, but money matters are not learned from איסור matters.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say: let us learn from it, we do not learn money laws from איסור laws.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא blocks a possible move. Someone might say: learn from the vows that the father also controls her money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Vows belong to the world of איסור, meaning what is permitted and forbidden. Money laws work by different rules, so the vow law cannot be stretched to give the father money rights.

keyTerms.meaning: We do not learn money matters from איסור matters

phrases.english: And if you say: let us learn from it,
phrases.notes: He means: learn from the father's power over her vows that he also gets her money.

phrases.english: we do not learn money matters from איסור matters.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends Step 13 against an expected objection.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The father's power over vows could teach his money rights.
steps.terutzMaskana: Money laws cannot be learned from איסור laws.

steps.title: Money laws are not learned from קנס
steps.stepSummary: One might learn from the קנס of a נערה, which goes to her father, but money laws are not learned from קנס.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say: let us learn from the קנס, we do not learn money laws from קנס.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא blocks a second possible source. This explains why רב needed the אמה פסוק after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה says the קנס paid for a נערה goes to her father. But a קנס is a special penalty that does not follow normal money rules, so nothing about ordinary money can be learned from it.

keyTerms.meaning: A קנס: a fixed Torah penalty
We do not learn money matters from a קנס

steps.whatToRemember: 'בנעוריה בית אביה' is about vows. A daughter's earnings go to her father because of the אמה פסוק, since money laws cannot be learned from איסור laws or from קנס.

phrases.english: And if you say: let us learn from the fine,
phrases.notes: The קנס paid for a נערה goes to her father (דברים 22:29).

phrases.english: we do not learn money matters from fines.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Blocks a second possible source, parallel to Step 14.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The father's right to the קנס could teach his right to her earnings.
steps.terutzMaskana: Money laws cannot be learned from קנס, so רב's אמה derivation is needed.

steps.title: No proof from humiliation and degradation payments
steps.stepSummary: One might try to learn from בושת ופגם, which go to the father. But the father has his own share in those payments, so no general money rule can be learned from them.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say: let us learn it from humiliation and degradation payments. Those are different, because her father also has a share in them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects one more possible source for giving the money to the father. It is the payments for בושת ופגם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בושת ופגם paid to the father could look like proof that a girl's money goes to him. But the father himself is shamed and hurt by what happened to her. So that money is partly his own, and it proves nothing about other money matters.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say (introduces a possible suggestion)
Has a connection to it, has a share in it

phrases.english: And if you would say: let us learn from humiliation and degradation —
phrases.notes: These are payments a man who violated her must make, and they are paid to her father.

phrases.english: humiliation and degradation are different,
because her father also has a share in it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of rejected possible sources from steps 14-15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the proposed source: the father has his own share in it
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The father receives בושת ופגם, so maybe all of a girl's money goes to him.
steps.terutzMaskana: בושת ופגם are partly the father's own loss, so no general rule can be learned from them.

steps.title: Back to the maidservant verse: it excludes only a comparable leaving
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the אמה העבריה source. When the תורה cuts out money for one kind of leaving, it cuts out only a comparable leaving. That shows that money does belong to the father in the comparable case of קידושין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is logical that when the Merciful One excludes, He excludes a leaving that is similar to it.
steps.whatsHappening: Since 'בנעוריה בית אביה' turned out to be only about vows, the challenge of step 10 needs a new answer. The גמרא goes back to רב יהודה's source from step 7, the אמה העבריה פסוק, and explains why the money it implies goes to the father and not to the girl herself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the maidservant leaves her master 'without money'. That exclusion speaks about a girl leaving someone's authority. So the money it implies must be for the matching case, a girl leaving her father's authority through קידושין, and that money goes to the one she leaves, the father.

keyTerms.meaning: It is logical, it makes sense
Leaving, going out of someone's authority

phrases.english: Rather, it is logical
that when the Merciful One excludes —
He excludes a leaving that is like it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 13 limited 'בנעוריה בית אביה' to vows, so step 11 no longer answers 'ואימא לדידה' (steps 8 and 10). The גמרא returns to רב יהודה's אמה העבריה source from step 7 and answers that question from the פסוק itself.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Logical reading of the scope of the exclusion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The money implied by the פסוק might belong to the girl herself.
steps.terutzMaskana: The exclusion is about a comparable leaving, so the money belongs to the father whose authority she leaves.

steps.title: The two kinds of leaving are not alike
steps.stepSummary: The maidservant leaves her master completely. A girl who receives קידושין still has not been handed over to the חופה, so her leaving is not complete. The two cases do not match.
steps.simpleTranslation: But this leaving is not like that leaving! There, with a master, she leaves his authority completely. The leaving from a father still lacks handing her over to the חופה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the comparison it just made. It says the maidservant's leaving and the daughter's leaving through קידושין are not really the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof depends on the two leavings being similar. A freed maidservant is totally out of her master's control. A betrothed girl is still partly under her father until the חופה. So maybe the פסוק does not speak about her case at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Handing her over to the wedding canopy

steps.confusionAlert: קידושין (betrothal) is not the same as being fully married. After קידושין the girl is still in her father's house until the חופה. That gap is exactly what this question is about.

phrases.english: But this leaving is not similar
phrases.notes: 'This leaving' is the girl leaving her father through קידושין.

phrases.english: to that leaving:
there, regarding a master,
she leaves his authority completely,
but leaving from a father —
still lacks handing over to the wedding canopy!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא לָא דָּמְיָא הָא יְצִיאָה לְהָא יְצִיאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the comparison made in step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 17 that the daughter leaving her father is a leaving comparable to the maidservant's.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The maidservant leaves completely, while a betrothed girl is still partly under her father until the חופה. The comparison fails.

steps.title: For vows, at least, she has left her father's control
steps.stepSummary: Through קידושין the girl does leave her father's sole control over vows. The משנה teaches that her father and her husband annul her vows together. That is enough to make the two leavings comparable.
steps.simpleTranslation: From annulling vows, at least, she leaves his authority. As we learned in a משנה: a betrothed נערה, her father and her husband annul her vows.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Through קידושין the girl really does leave her father's authority in one clear area, הפרת נדרים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before קידושין the father alone can annul her vows. After קידושין he cannot do it alone; he needs the husband together with him. So קידושין is a real leaving from the father's authority, and the comparison to the maidservant stands. This means the father does receive the קידושין money.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה

steps.whatToRemember: The father receives his daughter's קידושין money, learned from the אמה העבריה פסוק. This works because קידושין is a real leaving from the father's authority, at least for vows, where he can no longer annul them by himself.
steps.whyThisMatters: This closes the search for the source. It shows that even a partial leaving, like the loss of the father's sole power over vows, counts as a true leaving from his authority.

phrases.english: From annulment of vows, at least,
she leaves his authority,
as we learned in a משנה: a betrothed young woman —
her father and her husband annul her vows for her.
phrases.notes: Together. Her father can no longer do it on his own.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵהֲפָרַת נְדָרִים מִיהָא נָפְקָא לַהּ מֵרְשׁוּתֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 18 and saves the comparison of step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing that the leaving is real in one clear area (vows)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A betrothed girl has not truly left her father, so the maidservant's case is not comparable.
steps.terutzMaskana: Through קידושין she leaves her father's sole control over vows, so the two leavings are comparable and the father gets the קידושין money.
steps.raayaObject: That קידושין removes the girl from her father's sole authority.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in נדרים: a betrothed נערה's father and husband annul her vows together.

steps.title: Where do we learn that the father controls שטר and ביאה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a source that the father, and not only his daughter, can accept קידושין done through a document or through relations.
steps.simpleTranslation: Document and relations: from where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a source. We already know the father controls קידושין done with money, so how do we know he also controls קידושין done through a שטר or through ביאה?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier steps proved the father's rights only for כסף, because that proof was about money belonging to him. A שטר or ביאה is not money, so that proof does not cover them. A new source is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: A document. Here it means a written קידושין document handed to the woman.
Relations. One of the three ways to make קידושין.
From where do we know this? The standard way of asking for a source.

phrases.english: Document and relations: from where do we know?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the proof that כסף קידושין belongs to the father, the גמרא turns to the other two ways of making קידושין.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that the father also controls קידושין done through שטר and ביאה.

steps.title: All the ways of becoming a wife are compared to each other
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק ״וְהָיְתָה לְאִישׁ אַחֵר״ links all the ways a woman becomes a wife. So whatever is true of כסף is also true of שטר and ביאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: "And she becomes another man's wife." The ways of becoming a wife are compared to each other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק. The תורה speaks of a woman "becoming" a man's wife without naming one method, so all the methods are treated the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the פסוק links the methods together, a rule proven for one method carries over to the others. The father controls כסף קידושין, so he also controls קידושין through שטר and ביאה.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse says. Introduces a פסוק as the source.
They are compared to each other (from הֶקֵּשׁ, linking two things in the Torah).
Ways of becoming a wife, meaning the different methods of קידושין.

steps.whatToRemember: כסף, שטר, and ביאה are linked by ״וְהָיְתָה לְאִישׁ אַחֵר״. So the father's control over his daughter's קידושין covers all three methods.

phrases.english: The verse says: "And she becomes another man's wife,"
the ways of becoming a wife are compared to each other.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 20 with a פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק links all the methods of קידושין, so the father's control over כסף also covers שטר and ביאה.

steps.title: Quoting the next clause: the father gets what his daughter finds
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next part of the משנה, that the father is entitled to what his daughter finds, to start discussing it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He is entitled to what she finds.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next topic. It quotes the משנה's next clause about a daughter's מציאה so that it can discuss it next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line only quotes the משנה and decides nothing yet. The discussion of why the father gets her findings continues on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: Is entitled to; has the rights to.

phrases.english: He is entitled to what she finds —

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from קידושין to the next right the משנה gives the father.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The father is entitled to the items his daughter (a נערה) finds.
